measures.what_it_does: Lets the Forks school district, which reaches into Jefferson County's West End, issue $34 million in bonds repaid by property taxes over up to 25 years to replace the 1952 Forks Middle School with one secure building. The district says passing now brings about $21 million in state construction aid and keeps its timber revenue. Needs 60% plus minimum turnout.
measures.cost_line: District estimate: about $1.94 per $1,000 of assessed value, almost $680 a year on a $350,000 home, starting in 2028 as the high school bond is paid off. That bond's rate was $1.34 per $1,000 in 2025, in both counties.
measures.pro_summary: No statement in favor was filed. The district says the building fails current safety, seismic and energy codes, that replacing it costs less than remodeling, and that a November vote captures the most state matching money.
measures.con_summary: No statement against this measure was filed, and no opposing committee is listed.

taxes.basis: A yes vote authorizes a new 25-year excess property tax, estimated at $1.94 per $1,000, to repay $34 million. The district calls it a replacement for the expiring high school bond, the case for +1, but its estimate is above that bond's 2025 rate of $1.34.

measures.sources_note: Sources: the Jefferson local pamphlet, page 14 (S1); VoteWA record 7296 (S2); Peninsula Daily News and Forks Forum coverage (S3-S5); DOR 2025 levy detail (S6); a PDC query showing no committee (S7).

measures.what_it_does: Raises the Forks-area fire district's regular property tax from about $0.47 to $1.00 per $1,000 for 2027 collection; a small part of the district is in Jefferson County. For the next nine years the levy may grow with West Region inflation (at least 1%) instead of the usual 1% cap, up to the $1.50 legal maximum. Simple majority.
measures.cost_line: $1.00 per $1,000 in 2027, up from about $0.47: roughly $300 a year on a $300,000 property instead of $141. The Jefferson part paid $2,663 in 2025. Inflation-based increases follow through 2035.
measures.pro_summary: No statement in favor was filed. The district says inflation has outpaced the 1% limit for years and the levy is needed to keep current fire and EMS service and firefighter safety.
measures.con_summary: No statement against this measure was filed, and no opposing committee is listed.

taxes.basis: A yes vote more than doubles the district's regular levy rate, from about $0.47 to $1.00 per $1,000, and swaps the 1% growth limit for an inflation-based one for nine years. It stays within the $1.50 statutory cap, the case for +1.

measures.sources_note: Sources: the Jefferson local pamphlet, page 15 (S1); VoteWA record 7292 (S2); the Jefferson Elections page (S3); the Forks Forum (S4); DOR 2025 levy detail (S5); county GIS (S6); a PDC query showing no committee (S7). No statements for or against were filed.
